8. 1.
Mr. Parhi, learned advocate appears on behalf of petitioner and submits, the land acquired belongs to the deity.
Hence, his client has applied in name of the deity for interference of this Court in disbursement of the compensation to private opposite party nos. 1 to 9.

By order dated 26th April,
2023
there was direction upon the Commissioner to file the documents sought to be handed up, by way of affidavit.
The affidavit has since been filed.
In the affidavit there is clear assertion by the Commissioner that the institution stands indexed // 2 // but there is some minor variation in particular regarding area of the lands.
In the circumstances, his client's contention stands borne out by the Commissioner that the land acquired belong to the deity and therefore the compensation must also come to the deity.
2. Mr. Panigrahi, learned advocate appears on behalf of opposite party no.10 (Indian Oil Corporation).
He reiterates his submission that his client is in possession of the land, acquired for his client's benefit.
The compensation money has been deposited by his client.

1 3.
Mr. Nanda, learned advocate, Additional Government Advocate appears on behalf of State functionaries.
He submits, there was a civil suit filed by petitioner.
Opposite party nos. 1 to 9 or some of them had filed misc. case in the suit.
A revision arose from the civil suit and was disposed of by order dated 15 th September, 2015 of the learned single Judge.
Few paragraphs from said order are reproduced below.

"In my considered view, since the settlement of authorities have recorded the land in the name of Sri Sri Subarneswar Mahadeb, it was incumbent on the part of the Tahasildar to issue notice to the Endowment Commissioner before deleting the name of the deity from the Record Of Rights.

// 3 // Therefore, I hold that the Record of Rights issued in pursuance of Mutation Case No.5567 of 2012 is a nullity in the eye of law and, hence, the impugned order recording the case land in the name of O.P. Nos.1 to 9 is hereby quashed and the matter is remitted to the Tahasildar, Balasore, who shall make a de novo enquiry with regard to the status of the land and pass a reasoned order with regard to the ownership and possession of the land within a period of three months from the date of receipt of this order.
Since the Tahasildar, Balsore has to issue notice to the Commissioner of Endowment to appear before him, he shall also issue notice to the general public inviting objections with regard to status of the land.

The deposit made by the Land Acquisition Officer shall be kept in a Fixed Deposit till a decision is taken by the Tahasildar with regard to entitlement of O.P. Nos.1 to 9 in respect of the acquired land.
In view of the aforesaid order, the proceeding in Civil Suit No. 95 of 2014, which is pending before the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Balasore, has become infructuous.
Therefore, the said suit stands disposed of."
(emphasis supplied)
As such the civil proceedings stood disposed of on direction in said order.

He submits further, on restoration to the Tahsildar, the authority made order dated 25th August,
2016.
This order stands disclosed as annexure-E11 in counter filed by the Tahsildar.
The Tahsildar by said order upheld mutation of names of opposite party nos. 1 to 9 in the record, as purchasers.
Said order was not challenged by anybody.
5. Mr. Dash, learned advocate appears on behalf of opposite party nos. 1 to 9 and submits, his clients duly purchased the land, in their individual capacities, thereafter acquired.
Therefore, there must be distribution amongst them from the compensation money payable against acquisition of the land as a whole.

6. Mr. Parhi in response submits, the Tahsildar did not rely on evidence to record the land in names of opposite party nos. 1 to 9 as purchasers.
The alienation is itself questionable.
He submits, it was illegal.
He prays for interference.

7. The writ petition was presented on 15th March, 2016 in this Court, prior to the Tahsildar having had made said order dated 25 th August, 2016 reiterating the entries in the record in favour of opposite party nos. 1 to 9.
Such entries are at best a rebuttable presumption of claim and interest in the land, since acquired and compensation // 5 // therefor standing deposited with the appropriate authority.

As the civil suit stood disposed of by the learned single Judge on said order dated 15th September, 2015 without, the disputes raised therein having had been decided on merits, there can be no impediment for petitioner to once again approach the civil Court.
Petitioner will be entitled to seek exclusion of the time taken to prosecute the writ petition, for the purpose of limitation.

At this stage Mr. Nath submits, clause (d) under section 41(1) in Odisha Hindu Religious Endowments Act,
1951 empowers the Assistant Commissioner to decide on dispute regarding whether any property or money is of a religious endowment or specific endowment.
Mr. Parhi supports the contention while Mr. Nanda submits, it would be better for petitioner to approach the civil Court.

Mr. Das submits,
there should not be direction or option given to petitioner to approach the civil Court because the dispute stands resolved on restoration to the Tahsildar, aforesaid order dated 25th August, 2016 made and not challenged.
8.

We have already noticed that the writ petition was presented before said order dated 25th August,
2016 was passed by the Tahsildar, reiterating the entries in the record.
We accept Mr. Nanda's submission that it would be better for petitioner to approach the civil Court since, the Commissioner can be arraigned as a party, in it.
Interim order passed earlier will remain in force till six weeks from date, for petitioner to consider next course of action.
The interim order shall stand automatically vacated on expiry of six weeks from date, irrespective of steps taken by petitioner to agitate his contention before the appropriate forum.
Petitioner, if wants continuation of the protection, must obtain it from the forum approached.

We are making this order as the writ petition is found to be maintainable to extent that the civil proceeding was disposed of in the earlier writ petition, by the learned single Judge on order dated 15th September, 2015.
10. The writ petition is disposed of.
